levels.title: Potent Opioid Differentiation
levels.description: Differentiate high-potency synthetic opioids carrying catastrophic overdose risks.
levels.learningObjective: Differentiate fentaNYL and ALfentanil to prevent fatal opioid dosing errors.

lessons.title: Opioid Suffix & Prefix Recognition
lessons.learningObjective: Identify orthographic hazards between fentaNYL and ALfentanil.

activities.learningObjective: Identify clinical hazards between high-potency synthetic opioids.

questions.prompt: Why are fentaNYL and ALfentanil designated as high-alert LASA medications by ISMP?
choices: They have dramatically different potencies and rapid onset, where dosing confusion causes fatal respiratory depression
They are manufactured by the same pharmaceutical vendor with identical packaging
One is an over-the-counter cough syrup while the other is a topical patch
They share identical chemical structures with no clinical differences
questions.correctAnswer: They have dramatically different potencies and rapid onset, where dosing confusion causes fatal respiratory depression
questions.explanation: fentaNYL is an extremely potent opioid. Mix-ups with ALfentanil due to verbal orders or sound-alike names have caused catastrophic respiratory arrest.

questions.prompt: In the ISMP Tall Man lettering standard, fentaNYL capitalizes the suffix NYL while ALfentanil capitalizes the prefix AL.
questions.explanation: True. ISMP recommends fentaNYL (capitalizing NYL) and ALfentanil (capitalizing AL) to emphasize their distinct phonetic and orthographic ends.

activities.learningObjective: Independently construct the exact Tall Man lettering for high-potency fentanyl without scaffolding.

questions.prompt: Enter the complete medication name using exact Tall Man lettering to distinguish it from ALfentanil:
questions.explanation: fentaNYL capitalizes NYL to distinguish it from ALfentanil, which capitalizes AL.
